title: haplopappus uniflorus subsp. howellii
intro: Haplopappus uniflorus subsp. howellii, commonly known as Howell's rabbitbrush, is a plant species native to the western United States and Canada. It is used in herbal medicine for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which may help alleviate symptoms of colds, flu, and respiratory issues. The plant's therapeutic actions are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as sesquiterpene lactones and triterpenoids, which have been shown to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory activities. While more research is needed to fully understand the effects of Howell's rabbitbrush, its bioactive constituents may provide a natural alternative for managing various health conditions.
